blurb_title: The job reported success. Its retention had never worked.
blurb_1: This guide builds the backup for the OpenBao from Nº 1: a CronJob that logs in via ServiceAccount, takes the Raft snapshot, recomputes the archive's checksums and uploads to MinIO; a second one that raises the alarm when none arrived for 26 hours. Retention as a lifecycle rule on the bucket – not in the job, for good reason.
blurb_2: And a restore drill on an isolated second instance that shows the point everybody gets wrong the first time: restore -force leaves the instance sealed, the new key is rejected, only the original key unseals. With the real snapshot up to Total Shares 5.
code: -- Four steps, two key sets bao operator init # throwaway keys bao operator unseal <new key> bao operator raft snapshot restore -force prod.snap bao operator unseal <original-key> ×3 # the new ones are worthless
